record.original_question: Develop a theory of realizations of regular polytopes in hyperbolic spaces.

evidence.quote: Problem 35. Develop a theory of realizations of regular polytopes in hyperbolic spaces.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract regular polytope is a partially ordered set $P$ with a strictly monotone rank function, having a least and greatest face, satisfying the diamond condition and strong flag-connectedness, and whose automorphism group acts transitively on the set of maximal flags. For abstract regular polytopes in finite rank, McMullen developed a theory of (Euclidean) realizations: a realization is a mapping $\beta$ from the vertex set of $P$ into a Euclidean space $E$ such that the automorphism group of $P$ induces, via $\beta$, a representation by isometries of $E$ extending to an action on the resulting geometric figure. The full set of realizations of a finite regular polytope forms a convex cone, the realization cone, decomposing as a direct (Minkowski) sum of irreducible "pure" realizations indexed by the irreducible orthogonal representations of the automorphism group; an analogous, more delicate theory exists for infinite (Euclidean apeirotope) realizations.

Develop an analogous, systematic theory of realizations of abstract regular polytopes in hyperbolic spaces $\mathbb{H}^n$ (and possibly in other non-Euclidean spaces of constant curvature). In particular, define an appropriate notion of a hyperbolic realization of an abstract regular polytope $P$ as a map from the vertex set of $P$ into $\mathbb{H}^n$ that is compatible (in a suitable sense) with the action of the automorphism group of $P$ by hyperbolic isometries; identify the analogue of pure/irreducible realizations; describe the structure of the space of all hyperbolic realizations of a given regular polytope (e.g., is there an analogue of the realization cone, of the direct sum decomposition, and of the classification by irreducible representations?); and characterize which abstract regular polytopes admit faithful discrete realizations in hyperbolic spaces, recovering the classical hyperbolic regular tessellations and honeycombs as special cases.
artifact.status_search_result: A general theory of realizations of abstract regular polytopes in Euclidean space (McMullen) is well established, and individual hyperbolic regular tessellations/honeycombs are classically understood via hyperbolic Coxeter groups. However, no published systematic analogue of McMullen's realization theory in hyperbolic spaces appears to have been developed; recent surveys on symmetry of polytopes and on regular hypertopes continue to treat the hyperbolic setting only piecewise, suggesting the problem remains open.
